document_title: A Year After Halong, the Map Under the AI Forecast
post_copy:
NOAA's 16-day AI forecast now finishes in about 40 minutes. Y-K Delta airport stations have gone days or weeks with no observations.

Climatologist Rick Thoman told KYUK it has happened at every airport in the region since April.

NOAA fine-tuned that AI model on a grid of surface, balloon and satellite observations.

A year ago, global models had Halong's track and missed its shift east, Thoman said. A lack of balloon launches across Western Alaska may have played a role, KYUK reported.

NOAA's AI models went operational later, in December 2025.

A faster model can't fill in a reading nobody took.

Maps show the grid NOAA's AI model learned from, the Delta's dark stations, Halong's turn east and its saltwater on the tundra.

How much should the Delta trust a faster forecast while its own airport stations go days without a reading?

#YKDelta #AlaskaWeather #WeatherObservations

slides.headline: Forecasts now run on AI. The map under them has holes.
An AI forecast starts from a map of measurements.
slides.body: NOAA fine-tuned its AI model, AIGFS, on its own Global Data Assimilation System analyses. That system puts surface, balloon, aircraft, buoy, radar and satellite observations onto a three-dimensional grid.
labels: ILLUSTRATION · THE DELTA COAST NEAR KIPNUK · RELIEF 25X

slides.headline: Days or weeks with no observations.
slides.body: Since April, every airport weather station in the Y-K Delta region has gone days or weeks without observations at times, climatologist Rick Thoman told KYUK.
labels: 10 TO 15 OF EVERY 100 ALASKA AVIATION STATIONS DOWN OR NOT FULLY WORKING ON A GIVEN DAY, EXPERTS SAID

slides.headline: The models had the track. They missed the shift east.
slides.body: Global models forecast Halong's track into the Bering Sea well but failed to forecast its eastward shift, Thoman said. A lack of balloon launches across Western Alaska may have played a role, KYUK reported.
labels: NOAA'S AI MODELS WENT OPERATIONAL LATER, DECEMBER 17TH, 2025

slides.headline: Saltwater ran more than 15 miles onto the tundra.
slides.body: More than 1,500 people were forced from their homes. In Kipnuk, 90% of buildings were damaged or destroyed, KYUK reported.

slides.kicker: THE YEAR SINCE HALONG, AS A MAP LEGEND
slides.headline: What got faster. What went missing.
labels: NOAA SAYS V1.0 INTENSITY FORECASTS DEGRADED
Y-K DELTA AIRPORT STATIONS, DAYS OR WEEKS WITH NO OBSERVATIONS SINCE APRIL
MORE THAN 160 FAA STATIONS PROMISED, NO SITES NAMED AS OF APRIL

slides.headline: "Speed and skill are not the same as trustworthiness."
slides.body: AI sea ice forecast systems barely existed a decade ago and now number in the dozens, researchers wrote in Eos on October 9th. The observations needed to build and test them remain sparse across both poles.
labels: PASSIVE MICROWAVE SEA ICE RECORD SINCE 1978 · SWATHS ILLUSTRATED

slides.kicker: Thoman wants more than airport stations.
slides.headline: Where should Alaska's next observation go?
slides.body: "I'm not just talking more [FAA] weather stations."

showrunner_notes: Copywriter flags applied by the showrunner: C55 labels read 'down or not fully working' as the source does; C32 row reads 'intensity forecasts degraded'; slide 08's label says the swaths are illustrated; first comment no longer says 'we track'.
Slide 09's quote shortens KYUK's bracket [Federal Aviation Administration] to [FAA], brackets kept.
aftercare: Post when you choose. Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time, are the strongest slots; Tuesday October 20th to Thursday October 22nd keeps it close to KYUK's October 12th anniversary reporting.
Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting, as plain text, so every raw URL stays a working link. Pin nothing.
Reply to every comment in the first 60 minutes and keep answering through the first 90, especially pilots, forecasters, Y-K Delta residents and anyone who keeps a weather station running.
Expect one question. Did an AI model miss Halong? No. Thoman was describing global models in October 2025, and NOAA's AI models went operational December 17th, 2025.
At 48 hours, note this post's saves and comments so the next run's ledger and instincts learn from it.
editor_notes_for_email: The deck rests on one honesty guard. NOAA's AI models went operational December 17th, 2025, after Halong hit the Kuskokwim Delta coast on October 12th, 2025; slide 04's guard line and the caption both say 'later', and nothing claims an AI model forecast the storm. The station outages are Rick Thoman's account as KYUK paraphrased it, and the balloon line is KYUK's own 'may have played a role', attributed on slide 04 and in the caption.
